title: Exercise: Two-Hand Start
oneLiner: Run a press only while two buttons are held, pressed within half a second of each other, and refuse to restart until both are released.
keyTakeaway: A TON on LeftBtn OR RightBtn times the window from the first press and only resets when both are released; Press may start inside the window and then seals in while both are held.
explanation:
Presses and similar machines often use two-hand control: the operator must press two buttons, far enough apart to need both hands, at nearly the same time, and keep both pressed. That keeps the operator's hands out of the danger zone while the machine moves.

The logic is a good timing puzzle. It is also a good example of something a standard PLC program must not be trusted with on a real machine, as the good practice lesson explains: here it is practice only.
